I base these probabilities on the quality of different mathematical research efforts, the amount of funding available, and my confidence in the timeframe. I am uncertain and could be mistaken even about broad trends. I assume AI contributions are relevant if they improve on previous best work, so don't add any new insights. I assume the fastest possible solution requires roughly 10 years. If all six problems are still open in 2050, that means the fastest median solution took 2050-2040 = 10 years and is at least as hard as the median problem. I currently estimate it will be 10 years before AI is significantly faster than humans at solving most Millennium Problems that are still open in 2050.
